The other pilot’s failure to see and avoid the airplane, which resulted in a midair collision while both airplanes were on final approach to land.

The student pilot's failure to maintain adequate airspeed during night, adverse weather conditions, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall/spin. The partial loss of engine power during the initial climb due to the failure of both pilots to use carburetor heat during a long descent for landing in carburetor icing conditions, and, the flight instructor's inadequate supervision of the flight.
Fatigue cracking of the upper torque-link attach lugs on the left main landing gear strut, which resulted in separation of the left main landing gear during taxi.
The pilot's loss of control during landing for undetermined reasons.
The pilot’s failure to maintain directional control of the airplane during landing.
The pilot’s poor flight planning which resulted in a loss of engine power due to fuel exhaustion.
The pilot lost control of the airplane while on the ground due to temporary incapacitation.
A loss of engine power for undetermined reasons.
The pilot’s failure to maintain clearance from mountainous terrain during descent at night, with low clouds and fog.
An inadvertent collision with a deer on the runway during a night landing.
The pilot's mismanagement of the fuel supply, which resulted in fuel exhaustion. Contributing to the accident was improper preflight planning.
The flight instructor’s decision to remove the nosewheel chock while the engine was still operating.
The passenger’s inadvertent application of brakes during landing which resulted in a nose over.
The pilot’s improper in-flight fuel management, which led to fuel starvation and a total loss of engine power.

A loss of engine power due to degraded and incorrectly maintained ignition system components. Contributing to the accident was the pilot’s delay in turning the airplane towards the runway when the engine began to lose power.
The pilot's failure to maintain an adequate airspeed while landing.
The pilot's selection of an unsuitable takeoff area with an unfavorable wind.

The pilot’s failure to use carburetor heat in weather conditions conducive to carburetor icing, resulting in a partial loss of engine power and a forced landing during which the airplane struck an object and nosed over.
The pilot's failure to achieve a normal touchdown location and loss of directional control during landing roll out. Contributing to the accident were the runway's soft surface and short length.
The pilot's inadequate compensation for the crosswinds and failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll.
The pilot's inadequate compensation for the crosswind condition and failure to maintain directional control during the landing rollout.
The pilot's delayed decision to execute a go-around maneuver while landing with excess airspeed into a short strip, which resulted in a runway overrun and subsequent loss of control.
The pilot did not retract the landing gear before a water landing. Contributing to the accident was the pilot did not use a checklist.
A loss of engine power for undetermined reasons.
The non-instrument-rated pilot's decision to take off and fly into marginal weather conditions.
The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from a transmission wire.
The pilot’s decision to take off with the airplane over its maximum gross weight on a turf runway and with a tailwind, and his subsequent failure to maintain airplane control.
The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from a signpost during an aerial application flight.
A partial loss of engine power due to the substandard and incomplete maintenance of the engine.
The pilot’s loss of control for undetermined reasons.
The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during takeoff.
The pilot's inadequate visual lookout and failure to maintain clearance from a levy.
The loss of engine power due to improper maintenance by an unknown individual that led to the degradation and deterioration of the No. 2 piston, which was undetected because of overdue maintenance.
The flight instructor’s failure to maintain lateral control of the weight-shift-controlled aircraft during the landing flare.

The noninstrument-rated pilot’s decision to continue visual flight into instrument meteorological conditions, which resulted in his loss of aircraft control and the resultant overstress and in-flight breakup of the weight-shift-control aircraft.
The student pilot's failure to maintain directional control on landing. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's lack of flight experience.
The pilot's failure to maintain airspeed while maneuvering at low altitude, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall and impact with water.

A loss of engine power as a result of fuel exhaustion due to the pilot's improper decision to continue the flight after the low fuel warning. Contributing to the accident was the typographical error in the flight manual concerning the unusable fuel quantity.
The pilot's reconfiguration of the fuel venting system, which resulted in a loss of engine power and subsequent loss of aircraft control.

Fuel leaking from the fuel flow transmitter that ignited on contact with the engine’s hot cases which resulted in an engine undercowl fire. the pilot's failure to maintain correct airspeed and pitch attitude at touchdown.
The airplane's encounter with moderate turbulence at a higher altitude than the flight crew expected, resulting in an injury to a cabin crewmember.
The pilot’s inadvertent encounter with localized icing conditions and his subsequent in-flight loss of helicopter control.
The pilot’s mismanagement of rotor RPM and subsequent forced landing on uneven terrain which led to a dynamic rollover.
The pilot’s failure to maintain rotor rpm while maneuvering at low altitude with low airspeed and a tailwind.
